track_draft: Draft tracks from brief-v15-gap-audit 2.2 (rule: by kind and category) and 2.4 (audit: by judgment); not yet reviewed by a person.

items.name: Meilisearch
items.why_best: Single-binary, typo-tolerant instant search with a built-in web preview and simple REST API, much easier to run than Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and more popular than Typesense (60k vs 27k stars, MIT core vs GPL-3.0).

items.name: DBeaver Community
items.track_note: desktop GUI outside media_files/productivity_docs (gap audit 2.2, plan.md section 8)
items.why_best: The most widely used free universal SQL GUI (JDBC drivers for 80+ databases, ER diagrams, data import/export, cross-platform, Apache-2.0), far broader than Beekeeper Studio's community edition and free unlike DataGrip or TablePlus.

items.name: ClickHouse
items.why_best: The leading open-source columnar OLAP server (also ships clickhouse-local for one-shot queries on files), faster and more widely adopted for self-hosted analytics than Apache Druid or Apache Doris; the catalog only has its MCP server, not the database.

items.niche: Embedded/analytical SQL engine over local files
items.name: DuckDB
items.why_best: A single dependency-free binary that runs fast columnar SQL directly on CSV, Parquet and JSON files (and attaches SQLite/Postgres), which chDB and SQLite cannot match for local analytics; the catalog only has its in-browser WASM shell, not the native CLI that reads local files at full speed.

items.name: DB Browser for SQLite
items.track_note: desktop GUI outside media_files/productivity_docs (gap audit 2.2, plan.md section 8)
items.why_best: The standard free SQLite GUI (in apt, Homebrew, winget) that lets non-experts create, browse, edit and import/export SQLite files without writing SQL, which SQLiteStudio does with a smaller user base and generic tools like DBeaver do with far more setup.

items.name: pgcli
items.why_best: Drop-in replacement for psql with context-aware completion of tables and columns, syntax highlighting and pretty output, more ergonomic than psql and lighter than generic clients like usql that lack schema-aware completion.

items.niche: Publish / explore SQLite data as a web app and JSON API
items.name: Datasette
items.why_best: Turns any SQLite file into a browsable, filterable web UI plus JSON/CSV API with faceting and a plugin ecosystem, a job sqlite-web only half-covers (no API, no plugins) and that BI tools like Metabase are too heavy for.

items.name: dbmate
items.why_best: Framework-agnostic single-binary migration tool with plain SQL up/down files, create/drop/wait and schema.sql dump for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and ClickHouse, simpler than golang-migrate (no schema dump or db create) and fully MIT unlike Atlas, which gates features behind its Pro/login build.

items.name: Metabase
items.why_best: One jar/Docker image gives non-SQL users a query builder, charts and dashboards over most databases, far easier to stand up than Apache Superset or Redash (stale), with an AGPL open-source edition.

items.name: drawDB
items.why_best: Free, no-signup browser ER-diagram editor (self-hostable) that imports and exports SQL DDL for Postgres, MySQL, SQLite and more, with more stars and activity than ChartDB and no paywall unlike dbdiagram.io.

items.name: Dolt
items.why_best: A MySQL-compatible SQL database with Git-style branch, merge, diff and clone of data, the only mature tool in this niche now that datafold/data-diff is archived, and broader than table-diff tools like daff.

items.name: QuestDB
items.why_best: High-ingest time-series database queried with plain SQL plus a built-in web console, Apache-2.0 and a single Java binary, unlike InfluxDB 3 (new query model, enterprise split) or TimescaleDB (a Postgres extension, not a standalone install).

items.name: mycli
items.why_best: The MySQL counterpart of pgcli with schema-aware completion, highlighting and favorite queries, a clear upgrade over the stock mysql client and more focused than usql.

items.name: Adminer
items.why_best: A single PHP file (and official Docker image) that administers MySQL, Postgres, SQLite, MS SQL and more from a browser, much lighter than phpMyAdmin or pgAdmin (one database each) and longer-proven than CloudBeaver or WhoDB.

items.name: hl
items.why_best: Very fast pager/filter for JSON and logfmt logs (field filters, time ranges, follow mode, handles gigabyte files), more focused and faster on structured logs than lnav, and actively maintained unlike humanlog or angle-grinder.

items.name: Typst
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: A single static binary that compiles markup to PDF in milliseconds with incremental watch mode, readable errors and a real scripting language, versus a multi-GB TeX Live install with slow multi-pass builds; in Homebrew, winget, crates.

items.name: Paperless-ngx
items.why_best: The de facto self-hosted document archive: consumes scans/emails, OCRs them (Tesseract), auto-tags with learned matching and gives full-text search over the archive, with nothing comparable in maturity (Mayan EDMS is heavier and enterprise-oriented, Papra is young).

items.niche: Personal knowledge base, self-hosted plus desktop
items.name: Trilium Notes
items.why_best: The most complete self-hostable PKB: arbitrarily deep note tree with cloning, relation maps, per-note encryption, scripting, web clipper and sync between a Docker/single-binary server and the desktop app, where Joplin is flat notebooks and Logseq has no server.

items.name: Karakeep
items.why_best: The most complete self-hosted bookmark-everything app: links, notes and images with full-page archiving, full-text search (Meilisearch), optional AI tagging, browser extensions and mobile apps, where linkding is links-only and Wallabag is read-later only.

items.name: calibre
items.why_best: The uncontested ebook manager: library with metadata/cover download, conversion between EPUB/MOBI/AZW3/PDF/DOCX (ebook-convert CLI testable headless), device sync, editor and a built-in content server, where Calibre-Web and Kavita only serve an existing library.

items.name: BookStack
items.why_best: The standard easy self-hosted wiki: shelves/books/chapters/pages structure, WYSIWYG and Markdown editors, roles, revisions, built-in local login, and a well-known one-container image (with MySQL/MariaDB), MIT licensed, where Wiki.js 3 has stalled and Outline needs an external OAuth/OIDC provider and is BSL.

items.name: Zotero
items.why_best: The free, open-source research library: one-click capture via browser connector, PDF reader with annotations, CSL citations in 10,000+ styles and Word/LibreOffice/Pandoc plugins, where Mendeley is closed and Elsevier-locked and JabRef is BibTeX-only.

items.name: Marp CLI
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: Turns a plain Markdown file into HTML, PDF or PowerPoint slides in one `npx @marp-team/marp-cli` command with no project scaffolding, where Slidev needs a Vue/Node project and reveal.js is a library; fills the gap presenterm (terminal only) leaves.

items.name: Slidev
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The most popular developer slide tool: Markdown plus Vue components, live code highlighting/Monaco, presenter mode, recording and PDF/PPTX export, far richer than Marp when slides need interactivity.

items.name: SiYuan
items.why_best: Block-level references, embeds and SQL queries over notes with a Docker server and desktop apps, which differs from Trilium's tree model and is a more polished, actively-shipped block editor than Logseq's DB-version transition.

items.name: Docmost
items.why_best: Realtime collaborative block editor with spaces, permissions, comments and built-in diagrams (draw.io/Excalidraw/Mermaid) and local email/password login, AGPL, where Outline is BSL and needs an external auth provider; a different experience from BookStack's book structure.

items.name: Xournal++
items.why_best: The leading open-source pen-notes app with pressure-sensitive stylus input, PDF annotation, LaTeX formulas and layers on Linux/macOS/Windows, where Rnote has no PDF-first workflow and OneNote is closed.

items.name: nb
items.why_best: Plain-text notes, bookmarks, todos and wiki links with git-backed sync, encryption, full-text search and a local web view in one Bash script, more complete than zk (notes only) or jrnl (journal only).

items.name: Vikunja
items.why_best: Single Go binary with SQLite giving list, kanban, Gantt and table views, CalDAV and Todoist/Trello import, simpler to run than Planka (Postgres, kanban only) or WeKan (MongoDB).

items.name: mermaid-cli (mmdc)
items.why_best: The official offline renderer that turns .mmd files or Mermaid blocks in Markdown into SVG/PNG/PDF in scripts and CI, which the existing browser-based Mermaid Live Editor and server-based Kroki do not cover locally.

items.name: Immich
items.why_best: Immich is the de facto Google Photos replacement with mobile auto-backup, face recognition, map and smart search, with no paid tier, ahead of PhotoPrism (key features behind a paid membership) and LibrePhotos (much less active).

items.name: OBS Studio
items.why_best: OBS is the standard free recorder and streamer, with scenes, multiple sources, hardware encoding and plugins on Linux/macOS/Windows; vokoscreenNG and SimpleScreenRecorder only record and have no compositing.

items.name: FFmpeg
items.why_best: FFmpeg is the engine under HandBrake, yt-dlp, OBS and nearly every other media tool, and it alone covers convert, trim, remux, extract audio, scale and stream for every codec in one apt/brew/winget package.

items.name: Jellyfin
items.why_best: Jellyfin is the fully free media server with hardware transcoding, live TV and apps for every platform, while Plex and Emby are closed source and put features behind Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.

items.niche: File transfer between devices (CLI, any network)
items.name: croc
items.why_best: croc sends files or folders between any two machines over the internet with a code phrase, end-to-end encryption and resumable transfers in one static binary, where magic-wormhole needs Python and doesn't resume, and LocalSend only works on the same LAN.

items.name: OCRmyPDF
items.why_best: OCRmyPDF adds a searchable Tesseract text layer to scanned PDFs, outputs PDF/A, deskews and optimizes in one command, which raw Tesseract (images only) and pdfsandwich (unmaintained) can't do as well.

items.name: ImageMagick
items.why_best: `magick` reads and writes 200+ formats and does resize, crop, composite, watermark and batch `mogrify` in one CLI that every distro packages, which GraphicsMagick (slower releases) and libvips' vips CLI (fewer ops, terser docs) don't match for breadth.

items.name: qpdf
items.why_best: qpdf merges, splits, rotates, decrypts, linearizes and repairs PDFs without touching content, is in every package manager, and is the reference tool behind OCRmyPDF/pikepdf, whereas pdftk-java is a Java port and pdfcpu is younger and less widely packaged.

items.name: copyparty
items.why_best: copyparty is one Python file that serves resumable uploads, WebDAV, FTP, SMB, media thumbnails and dedup with accounts, much more than miniserve (already listed) or dufs, and it is still maintained while File Browser was archived in 2026.

items.name: Czkawka
items.why_best: Czkawka (with its CLI and Krokiet GUI) finds duplicate files, similar images and videos, broken files and empty folders fast in Rust, a broader set than fdupes (exact duplicates only) or dupeGuru (slow, barely maintained).

items.name: Squoosh
items.why_best: Squoosh compresses images in the browser with MozJPEG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL and OxiPNG, shows a side-by-side quality slider and never uploads files, which TinyPNG (uploads, quota) and Caesium (desktop only) don't offer.

items.name: Navidrome
items.why_best: Navidrome streams a personal music library through a web UI and the Subsonic API (works with dozens of mobile clients) from one light Go binary, lighter than Jellyfin for music and better maintained than Airsonic-Advanced.

items.name: gallery-dl
items.why_best: gallery-dl is the yt-dlp of image sites, supporting 300+ sites (Pixiv, Reddit, Instagram, DeviantArt, Danbooru) with an archive file and config-driven naming, which yt-dlp doesn't handle and RipMe (Java, slower) only partly covers.

items.name: beets
items.why_best: beets auto-tags and organizes music against MusicBrainz, fetches art and lyrics and transcodes through plugins, all scriptable from the CLI, unlike MusicBrainz Picard (GUI) or puddletag (manual tagging).

items.name: ExifTool
items.why_best: ExifTool reads and writes EXIF/XMP/IPTC and maker notes for far more formats than exiv2 or exiftran, and its batch rename-by-date and GPS stripping are what photographers and privacy guides point to.

items.name: Caddy
items.why_best: Automatic HTTPS (ACME issuance and renewal) by default and a three-line Caddyfile, where nginx (already listed) needs certbot and longer config and Traefik is built around Docker/Kubernetes label discovery; one static binary that serves on a high port as a normal user.

items.name: Grafana
items.why_best: The default dashboard for Prometheus, Loki, Postgres and 100+ data sources with alerting built in, far broader than Kibana (Elasticsearch-only) or Chronograf (InfluxDB-only); the standalone tarball runs as a normal user with SQLite on :3000.

items.name: Ansible
items.why_best: Agentless (only SSH and Python on the target) with the largest module and Galaxy collection ecosystem, which Salt and Puppet/Chef cannot match without installing agents or a master; a playbook against localhost runs as a normal user from pipx.

items.name: Prometheus
items.why_best: The CNCF-graduated standard for pull-based metrics and PromQL that nearly every exporter, Kubernetes and Grafana speak natively; VictoriaMetrics is leaner but is PromQL-compatible precisely because Prometheus is the reference, and Zabbix is heavier and agent-centric; a single static binary that scrapes itself on :9090 as a normal user.
items.note: the catalog's prometheus has the same name but another repo

items.name: Podman
items.why_best: Docker-compatible CLI that runs containers without a daemon and without root, which Docker Engine (root daemon) and nerdctl (needs containerd) do not, so it is the container tool most likely to work in pickfit's no-Docker, no-root sandbox; the repo moved from containers/podman (redirect), and rootless runs need user namespaces plus newuidmap, so verification may fall back to `podman info`/`podman build` if the sandbox kernel blocks them.

items.name: OpenTofu
items.why_best: The Linux Foundation fork of Terraform that stays open source (MPL-2.0) and reads the same HCL and providers, so it beats Terraform (BSL since 1.6, not open source) on license and Pulumi on reach, since most IaC examples and modules are written in HCL; `tofu init/plan` with the local or null provider runs as a normal user with no cloud account.

items.name: Helm
items.why_best: The CNCF-graduated package manager that Artifact Hub charts are published for, and the binary pickfit's listed helmfile drives; Kustomize only patches YAML and has no packaging, versioning or rollback; `helm create`, `helm lint` and `helm template` run offline without a cluster.

items.niche: Real-time single-host monitoring agent with web UI
items.name: Netdata
items.why_best: Per-second metrics with thousands of auto-detected collectors and a ready dashboard with no configuration, which Glances (fewer collectors) and Beszel (listed, lightweight host stats) do not offer; the static installer can run as a normal user, though some collectors want root, and the cloud sign-in is optional.

items.name: Coolify
items.why_best: The most complete self-hosted Heroku/Vercel replacement (deploy on commit, databases, one-click services, multiple servers, backups) with the largest community, more featureful than Dokku (CLI-only) and more established than Dokploy (non-standard license); its installer needs root and Docker, so it cannot be verified in today's sandbox and needs a full VM.

items.name: Grafana Loki
items.why_best: Indexes only labels, so it is far cheaper to run than Elasticsearch/OpenSearch or Graylog (which needs MongoDB plus OpenSearch), and it plugs straight into Grafana with LogQL; single-binary mode with filesystem storage runs as a normal user.

items.name: kind
items.why_best: The Kubernetes project's own tool for multi-node clusters in containers, used to test Kubernetes itself, lighter than minikube's VM drivers and closer to upstream than k3d (which runs k3s); needs Docker or rootless Podman, so it is hard to verify in the current sandbox without a container runtime.

items.name: Kopia
items.why_best: A deduplicating, encrypted backup tool that ships both a CLI and a desktop/web UI (KopiaUI) with policies and scheduling built in, which restic (listed, CLI only, no scheduler) and BorgBackup (SSH/local repos only, no native cloud backends) lack; `kopia repository create filesystem` works as a normal user.

items.name: Healthchecks
items.why_best: Dead-man's-switch monitoring for cron jobs and backups (alerts when a ping does not arrive) with cron-expression schedules and 25+ notification integrations, a job Uptime Kuma's push monitors cover only thinly and Cronitor does not offer self-hosted; a Django app that runs with SQLite as a normal user.

items.name: Woodpecker CI
items.why_best: A lightweight community fork of Drone that stayed Apache-2.0 (Drone went source-available) with YAML pipelines and Gitea/Forgejo/GitHub integration, far lighter than Jenkins; server plus agent with the `local` backend can run without Docker, but a real pipeline needs a forge to connect to.

items.name: Headlamp
items.why_best: An official Kubernetes SIG project that runs both as a desktop app and as an in-cluster web UI with a plugin system, replacing the retired Kubernetes Dashboard and avoiding Lens's account wall (Freelens is the community fork but desktop-only); needs a cluster to show anything, so pair it with kind.

items.name: Vaultwarden
items.why_best: Lightweight Rust server compatible with all official Bitwarden apps and the web vault (pickfit already lists the Bitwarden clients), running in tens of MB of RAM versus the official multi-container Bitwarden server; Passbolt is team-only and heavier.

items.name: Headscale
items.why_best: Self-hosted Tailscale control server that works with the official Tailscale clients on every OS, so users get WireGuard mesh networking without a vendor account; NetBird and ZeroTier self-hosting need more moving parts and their own clients. Sandbox: the server runs as a normal user; clients would need TUN/root or tailscaled --tun=userspace-networking.

items.name: Nuclei
items.why_best: Single Go binary with ~10k community-maintained YAML templates for CVEs and misconfigurations, faster and far more current than Nikto, and scriptable in CI unlike OpenVAS's heavy server stack. Sandbox needs a local HTTP target to scan.

items.niche: Static analysis (SAST) for security bugs in source code
items.name: Semgrep
items.why_best: Runs offline on 30+ languages with readable pattern rules and thousands of community security rules, much easier to adopt than CodeQL (needs a database build, restricted license) and broader than Bandit (Python only).

items.name: Nmap
items.why_best: The decades-old reference scanner with service/version detection and the NSE script library, packaged in every distro and Homebrew; RustScan and masscan are faster port sweepers but hand off to nmap for detection. Sandbox note: no root means TCP connect scans (-sT) and -sV only; SYN scans and OS detection need raw sockets.

items.name: testssl.sh
items.why_best: Pure bash + bundled openssl, checks protocols, ciphers, certificate chain and known TLS vulnerabilities on any port including STARTTLS, without sending data to a third party the way the SSL Labs web test does; more complete report than sslyze. Sandbox: test against a local openssl s_server or a public host.

items.name: AdGuard Home
items.why_best: Single Go binary DNS server with web UI, DoH/DoT/DoQ upstreams and encrypted DNS serving built in, where Pi-hole needs a root installer and extra pieces for encrypted DNS. Sandbox: bind DNS to a high port since port 53 needs root.

items.name: Lynis
items.why_best: Agentless shell script that runs hundreds of hardening checks on Linux/macOS/BSD with a hardening index and suggestions, much lighter than OpenSCAP's SCAP content workflow. Sandbox: runs as a normal user with a reduced set of checks.

items.name: ZAP
items.track_note: desktop GUI outside media_files/productivity_docs (gap audit 2.2, plan.md section 8)
items.why_best: The free, open-source DAST standard with spider, active scanner and headless baseline/API scan modes, where Burp Suite's scanner requires the paid Pro edition; complements mitmproxy, which only inspects traffic. Sandbox: headless daemon mode needs only Java; GUI needs a display.

items.name: OSV-Scanner
items.why_best: Google's scanner on the OSV.dev database covering 20+ ecosystems' lockfiles, with call-graph reachability and guided remediation that Trivy and Grype lack; P1 because Trivy (already listed) also scans lockfiles.

items.name: OpenBao
items.why_best: Linux Foundation open-source fork of HashiCorp Vault under MPL-2.0 (Vault moved to BUSL), API-compatible with Vault clients; Infisical is more app-focused and its enterprise features are paywalled. Sandbox: `bao server -dev` runs in memory as a normal user.

items.name: ClamAV
items.why_best: The only widely deployed open-source antivirus engine, with freshclam signature updates and clamscan for files, mail and uploads; commercial engines are closed and YARA needs you to bring your own rules. Sandbox: freshclam downloads a ~300 MB signature database.

items.name: zizmor
items.why_best: Fast Rust analyzer that finds template injection, over-broad permissions and unpinned actions in workflows, with an offline mode; actionlint checks syntax rather than security, and Scorecard grades whole repos rather than pinpointing workflow lines.

items.name: Cosign
items.why_best: The Sigstore reference tool for signing and verifying container images and blobs, supported by every major registry and Kubernetes policy engine; Notation has far less adoption and GPG signing does not attach to OCI images. Sandbox: key-pair signing works offline; keyless mode needs OIDC.

items.name: ssh-audit
items.why_best: Reports weak key exchange, host key and cipher algorithms with fix-it hardening guides and policy checks for both servers and clients; nmap's ssh2-enum-algos script only lists algorithms without judging them.

items.niche: AI coding agent in the terminal
items.name: opencode
items.why_best: The most-starred open-source terminal coding agent (MIT, provider-agnostic: Anthropic, OpenAI, local models), actively shipped daily, unlike Aider which has not been pushed since May 2026 and Codex CLI which centers on OpenAI models.

items.name: Neovim
items.why_best: The most-used terminal editor today: Vim compatible, with built-in LSP client, Tree-sitter and Lua plugins, in every package manager; pickfit has no editor at all, and Vim and Emacs lack its built-in LSP/Lua ecosystem out of the box.

items.name: uv
items.why_best: One fast Rust binary replacing pip, pip-tools, virtualenv, pipx and pyenv with lockfiles and Python installs, now the default recommendation over Poetry and pipx; mise covers runtime versions but not Python dependency resolution.

items.name: Ruff
items.why_best: A single Rust binary that lints (800+ rules) and formats Python 10-100x faster than the tools it replaces, so one tool does what Flake8 plus Black (plus isort) used to.

items.name: tmux
items.why_best: The standard multiplexer preinstalled or one apt/brew away on every server, with detachable sessions over SSH and a huge plugin/config ecosystem; zellij (already listed) is friendlier but far less ubiquitous, and GNU screen is barely developed.

items.name: ShellCheck
items.why_best: The de facto static analyzer for bash/sh scripts, with explained warning codes and editor/CI integrations everywhere; no real alternative matches its rule depth (shfmt only formats, bashate only checks style).

items.name: Helix
items.why_best: A modal editor with LSP, Tree-sitter and multiple cursors working out of the box with zero config, a very different experience from Neovim's plugin-assembled setup and more active than Kakoune.

items.name: pre-commit
items.why_best: The most widely adopted git-hook framework, with thousands of ready hooks pinned per repo in .pre-commit-config.yaml and managed per-language environments, which Husky (JS-only) and Lefthook (smaller hook ecosystem) do not match.

items.niche: Self-hosted chat web UI for local models
items.name: Open WebUI
items.why_best: The most-used self-hosted ChatGPT-style UI (159k stars) with native Ollama and OpenAI-compatible backends, multi-user accounts, built-in RAG, web search and tools in one pip/Docker install, far more complete than the small UIs pickfit lists.

items.niche: Run GGUF LLMs locally (engine CLI + OpenAI-compatible server)
items.name: llama.cpp
items.why_best: The reference GGUF engine that Ollama, LM Studio and most catalog entries wrap; llama-cli/llama-server give the newest model support, every quant type and CPU/CUDA/Vulkan/Metal backends first, and it is in Homebrew/winget; a 0.5B Qwen GGUF on CPU proves it.

items.name: vLLM
items.why_best: The de facto production LLM server (PagedAttention, continuous batching, OpenAI-compatible API, broad model support) with far larger community than SGLang or TGI; show it on a T4/L4 with Qwen2.5-0.5B in fp16 (T4 has no bf16; large models >24 GB VRAM out of scope).

items.niche: Local RAG / chat with your documents
items.name: AnythingLLM
items.why_best: All-in-one document chat with workspaces, built-in vector DB (LanceDB), local embedder and agent tools, shipped as Docker server and desktop app, so no assembly is needed unlike PrivateGPT or Khoj.

items.name: Piper
items.why_best: Fast CPU-only neural TTS (pip install piper-tts) with dozens of languages and small ONNX voices, used by Home Assistant; the continued home after rhasspy/piper was archived, and lighter than Coqui TTS (abandoned) or Kokoro servers.

items.name: Upscayl
items.track_note: desktop GUI outside media_files/productivity_docs (gap audit 2.2, plan.md section 8)
items.why_best: The leading free desktop upscaler (Linux AppImage/Flatpak, Windows, macOS) wrapping Real-ESRGAN ncnn-Vulkan with batch mode and bundled models; Real-ESRGAN itself has not been pushed since 2024 and has no GUI. Needs a Vulkan GPU (T4/L4 fine).

items.name: rembg
items.why_best: The most-used offline background remover: CLI, HTTP server and batch folder mode over U2Net/BiRefNet/ISNet ONNX models on CPU, with no account, beating GUI-only tools like backgroundremover or web services like remove.bg.

items.name: LibreTranslate
items.why_best: The standard self-hosted translation API and web UI (Argos Translate models, CPU-only, pip or Docker), with a stable REST API many apps integrate, unlike desktop-only or single-language-pair tools.

items.name: Home Assistant
items.why_best: Local-first hub with 2,000+ integrations, automations and dashboards and by far the largest community, well past openHAB and Domoticz in device coverage and release pace.

items.name: uBlock Origin
items.track_note: human tool outside the three tracks; deferred pending review (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The de facto content blocker: wide-spectrum filter lists, element picker, dynamic filtering and low memory use, fully free with no 'acceptable ads' deal, unlike AdBlock Plus or the freemium AdGuard extension.

items.name: Actual Budget
items.why_best: Local-first envelope budgeting (YNAB-style) with sync, bank import and rules under MIT; lighter and easier to start with than Firefly III's double-entry ledger, and more modern than GnuCash.

items.name: SearXNG
items.why_best: Actively maintained fork of the abandoned searx that pulls results from 200+ engines with no tracking or profiling; broader than single-site front-ends like Redlib or Invidious.

items.name: FreshRSS
items.why_best: Most popular self-hosted reader: multi-user, extensions, WebSub, and the Google Reader/Fever APIs that mobile apps use; more features than minimalist Miniflux and more active than Tiny Tiny RSS.

items.name: Espanso
items.track_note: human tool outside the three tracks; deferred pending review (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: Cross-platform (Linux X11/Wayland, macOS, Windows) text expander with YAML configs and a package hub; free and open, unlike TextExpander, and not tied to one OS like AutoHotkey.

items.name: Thunderbird
items.track_note: human tool outside the three tracks; deferred pending review (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The standard free cross-platform mail client, with IMAP/POP/Exchange (EWS), built-in calendar, contacts and OpenPGP; more complete than Mailspring or Evolution on every OS.
items.verified: curl -sI https://www.thunderbird.net returned HTTP 302 on 2026-11-20; source mirror thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop pushed 2026-11-20 (gh api, 254 stars, license unset on GitHub, MPL-2.0 per project)

items.name: Blender MCP
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The most-installed creative-app MCP server by far (35k stars): a Blender add-on plus MCP bridge that creates and edits scenes, materials and Python in a free local Blender, where the alternatives are small forks or project-specific harnesses.

items.niche: Multi-database gateway (many engines through one server)
items.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
items.why_best: One Go binary (also in Homebrew) that serves Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, Redis, Neo4j, BigQuery and dozens more with connection pooling, auth and tools defined in YAML; it has far more engines and much more maintenance than the small multi-database servers pickfit lists now. A local SQLite source makes it verifiable with no services.

items.name: Framelink Figma MCP (Figma-Context-MCP)
items.why_best: The default design-to-code MCP server (16k stars): it trims Figma's REST response down to layout and style data an agent can use, works with a free Figma account's personal token, and runs locally via npx, unlike Figma's own Dev Mode server, which needs the desktop app and a paid seat.

items.name: Excel MCP Server
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The leading spreadsheet MCP server (4.3k stars): it creates and edits .xlsx with formulas, charts, pivot tables and formatting through openpyxl, with no Excel install needed, while sbroenne/mcp-server-excel needs Windows and Excel, and document readers only read.

items.name: GhidraMCP
items.why_best: The best-known reverse-engineering MCP server (12k stars): a Ghidra plugin plus Python bridge that lets an agent decompile, rename and list functions in the NSA's free Ghidra, where the newer forks have a fraction of its users.

items.name: Mobile MCP
items.why_best: The standard mobile counterpart to Playwright MCP (10.7k stars): it drives Android emulators, iOS simulators and real devices through accessibility trees with a screenshot fallback, where the alternatives are single-platform or Frida-only tools.

items.name: Zotero MCP
items.track_note: document or creative tool with an agent interface (gap audit 2.4)
items.why_best: The clear Zotero MCP server (6k stars): it searches, reads annotations and full text, and does semantic search across a library through the local Zotero API or the free web API, where the alternatives are small native or plugin variants.

items.niche: Web search and scraping (self-hosted, no API key)
items.name: mcp-searxng
items.why_best: The most-used SearXNG bridge (1.4k stars, in the awesome lists): private, key-free web search plus URL-to-markdown reading against a self-hosted SearXNG, which fills the gap left by pickfit's search servers (Brave, Exa, Firecrawl), all of which need a vendor API key.
